newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police seek East Timorese rioters.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police seek East Timorese rioters.

text.p: Indonesian police in East Timor said on Sunday they were still looking for an unspecified number of suspects from a riot in the enclave of Ambeno last week in which one Moslem migrant died.

"The situation was quickly controlled on Friday and we are now looking for the perpetrators, who will be processed according to the law," acting East Timor police chief Colonel John Papalangi told Reuters by telephone from the territory's capital Dili.
The Jakarta Post newspaper on Saturday said 30-year-old Mahmud Abuh was stabbed to death when about 6,000 people rioted East Timor on Friday morning.
Papalangi confirmed the dead man was a trader from South Sulawesi province but gave no further details.
The local regent, Filomeno Da Costa Misquita, said the rioters burnt 86 houses and six vehicles in Pantai Makasar, the main town in the enclave about 200 km (124 miles) west of Dili.
Residents and authorities in Ambeno could not be contacted on Sunday.

Residents said on Friday the violence by local Catholic East Timorese was directed towards Buginese Moslem migrants from South Sulawesi after local people became enraged by a slight against a Catholic priest on Wednesday evening.
The Jakarta Post said that during a post-Ramadam function at the local Ambeno military base, a Catholic priest was given a dinner-box containing leftover food.

"The case is still under investigation. It is not yet clear what triggered the riot as the problem at the dinner had already been solved as the local regent, military chief and police chief had all apologised to the priest and he accepted it," Papalangi said.

In recent years there has been on-going tension between predominantly Catholic East Timorese and migrants from mostly Moslem Indonesia. The migrants dominate the economic life of the former Portuguese colony, invaded by Indonesia in 1975.
Ambeno is an enclave on the western half of Timor island, part of Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara province, which had been under Portuguese rule and is still administered from East Timor.
The United Nations has never recognised Jakarta's annexation of East Timor and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
